inputs.coverage: No image resolves the nucleus. Hubble limits its radius to at most 0.5 km at assumed geometric albedo 0.04, and its non-gravitational acceleration requires at least 0.2 km at assumed density 500 kg/m³ (Jewitt et al. 2020). Hui et al. (2020) estimate it is most likely at most 0.4 km. The display is a 0.4 km sphere: an estimate inside those bounds, not a measured size or shape. Pole RA 205°, Dec 52° (obliquity 30°), fitted to coma anisotropy by Kim et al. (2020); the prime meridian and spin phase are arbitrary and the period is not determined. The grid marks unmapped terrain.
